thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Canary rollout 0.12 -> v2-quant triggered high error rate and automatic sticky fallback in eu-west-1. Paging oncall.
jamie_sre: oncall ack, looking. can you post the incident link and approx error %? :wave:
noah_ml_oncall: seeing 5xxs spike from 00:12 UTC, ~12% failed requests for chat/generation route. latency up too. metric link: https://grafana.redwood/team-inference/d/xyz
rachel_eng: confirming this is the canary we pushed at 00:10 (v2-quant, quantized int8). any early logs pointing to OOM or kernel failures?
noah_ml_oncall: logs show "KV cache OOM" and then gateway returns 502 for some pods. stack traces point to serving runtime rejecting kv-resize. cc @ben_infra
ben_infra: I see pod restarts on eu-west-1-gpupool-3; node logs show out-of-memory on nvidia container. but CPU high too. not seeing similar in us-east-1.
carla_sre: sticky fallback policy kicked in—many sessions moved to fallback variant but affinity kept them assigned; seems fallback mapping was configured to fallback -> canary-compat which mistakenly points at v2-quant. so ansible config mismatch?
luke_pm: wait, fallback should go to stable (v1) not canary. that would explain loop. can we confirm policy mapping?
jamie_sre: checking control plane policies... (snippet)

```
GET /policies/smart-routing/active
response: {
  "traffic_routes": [
    {"tag":"canary","variant":"v2-quant","sticky_affinity":true},
    {"tag":"fallback","variant":"v2-quant","sticky_affinity":true}
  ]
}
```

jamie_sre: yep, fallback variant is incorrectly set to v2-quant. likely a deploy-time templating bug.
ash_support: customer-impact: reported by 3 mid-market customers in eu, intermittent 502s on chat endpoints. estimated ~3500 requests failing in last 10m.
rachel_eng: immediate mitigation: disable sticky fallback and revert fallback variant to v1-stable, then pause the canary rollout. who can flip that config quickly?
ben_infra: I can flip policy and pause rollout. plan:
1) PATCH control-plane /policies/smart-routing -> set fallback.variant = "v1-stable" and sticky_affinity=false
2) PATCH /rollouts/{canary}/actions -> pause
3) scale down canary replicas to zero in eu-west-1
I'll run steps now.

ben_infra: ran step 1 & 2. awaiting confirmation from control-plane (200 OK).
jamie_sre: control-plane confirmed policy update. new policy diff:
```
fallback: v1-stable, sticky_affinity: false
```
jamie_sre: pausing rollout confirmed.
ben_infra: scaling down canary pods in eu-west-1... scaled to 0. node memory usage returning to normal.
noah_ml_oncall: error rate dropped to 0.6% in 2m. latency trending down. looks good.
ash_support: note to support team: customers A,B,C notified. PR to incident page started.
luke_pm: root cause hypothesis: templating bug in deployment pipeline that substituted canary variant into fallback block when variable not scoped. need to add validation for fallback variant not equal to canary.
rachel_eng: agree. action items: 
- short: add CI check to validate policy mapping (jenkins job)
- medium: add runtime guard to prevent fallback and canary pointing to same variant
- long: telemetry to detect fallback-target == canary on deploy and auto-block
carla_sre: creating followup ticket INFRA-3421 and assigning to eng/runtime + infra. include logs and timestamps.
jamie_sre: will run a postmortem template. can we keep the channel for updates until EOD? :+1:
noah_ml_oncall: one more note: we should also audit other regions for the same templating bug. running quick grep across manifests.
ben_infra: grep finished, only the eu manifest had the wrong variable. likely template scoping bug on region-specific overlay.
ash_support: customers asked for ETA; we advised we paused rollout and reverted policies, monitoring now. next update in 30m.
incident-bot: incident severity set to sev2. pagers notified: oncall, infra, ml-oncall. incident channel will remain open until resolved.
carla_sre: closing actions: rollback completed, policy fixed, ticket opened. leaving channel open for postmortem notes.
jamie_sre: thanks everyone. final metric snapshot and timeline will be posted to the incident doc. :thumbsup:
